record.office: Acting Speaker, Kentucky House of Representatives
record.t: Was set to become acting speaker of the Kentucky House following the resignation of Jeff Hoover.
record.q: But Wednesday evening, The Courier-Journal reported the settlement, based on anonymous sources, which eventually led to Hoover’s resignation. Hoover said he will remain in the legislature. House Speaker Pro Tempore David Osborne will become the acting speaker.

record.t: Ruled that Jeff Hoover's resignation had been accepted by the House.
record.q: Moments after Jeff Hoover offered Monday to resign — but only if the House would accept — Speaker Pro Tem David Osborne ruled that his resignation had been accepted.

record.t: Said the House would not officially have a speaker for the rest of the session and that he would keep presiding as speaker pro tem until his term in that office ends at year's end.
record.q: Meanwhile, Osborne said the House won’t officially have a speaker for the remainder of this session, but he will continue to preside as speaker pro tem until his term in that office expires at the end of this year.

record.t: Joined three other House GOP leaders in a statement asking caucus members who believe they will be implicated in the matter to inform the leadership team immediately.
record.q: “We are asking any member of the House Republican caucus who is or believes they will be implicated in this matter to inform this leadership team immediately if their name has not already surfaced in the public domain,” according to a statement attributed to Osborne and three other House GOP leaders.

record.office: Speaker of the Kentucky House of Representatives
record.t: Took the microphone from Rep. Thomas Massie during Massie's speech at a GOP dinner in Massie's district.
record.q: Massie was saying he works for the people of his district, rather than Trump or House Speaker Mike Johnson (R-LA), when Republican Kentucky House Speaker David Osborne snatched his microphone.
